name: Gameface
label: Revelation
lede: Four Orange County kids who met in the pit lost their drummer in 1994, kept going as his memorial, and grew into the warmest-sounding band on late-'90s Revelation.

eras.title: The rhythm section from the pit
eras.text: Jeff Caudill and Todd Trout kept seeing the same two faces at Orange County punk shows, and in 1990 they made them a band. Gameface grew up on R.E.M., the Descendents and Buffalo Tom, put out 7"s and a first album, and then, in the summer of 1994, lost their drummer.

years.h: Gameface form out of the Orange County punk crowd
years.p: Jeff Caudill and Todd Trout recruit Paul Martin and Bob Binckley, two regulars they kept running into at local shows. Martin takes bass and Binckley drums.

years.h: Gameface's first 7" on Nemesis Records
years.p: Gameface's self-titled debut 7" comes out on Nemesis Records, with the band tagged as O.C. power pop. The Beach Chair 7" follows in 1992.

years.h: Good, Gameface's first album · Network Sound
years.p: Gameface's debut full-length comes out on Network Sound, the only album with the original four.

years.big: They kept the band as his memorial
q: We dealt with it by writing songs
years.src: Dying Scene · No Echo · Revelation Records
years.h: Gameface drummer Bob Binckley dies by suicide
years.p: Bob Binckley, Gameface's original drummer, died by suicide in the summer of 1994. The other three decided to keep Gameface going in his memory.
years.xp:
Todd Trout told Dying Scene in 2025 that Binckley went to a gas station one afternoon, bought gas, sat down and set himself on fire. Trout remembered it happening around the time of the O.J. Simpson chase.

Jeff Caudill told No Echo the band dealt with it the only way it knew.

eras.title: Three to get ready
eras.text: Gameface came back with a drummer who had a big mohawk and fast hands, and a record whose title track is about the friend they lost. Then Steve Sanderson arrived, Caudill picked up a second guitar, and the band's songs opened up.

years.h: Three to Get Ready, Gameface's comeback · Dr. Strange
years.p: With new drummer Phil Hansen, Gameface make their return on Dr. Strange Records. The title track is about Bob Binckley's death.
years.xp: Caudill and Trout remember Hansen as a lightning-fast drummer with a big mohawk. Dr. Strange's owner, Bill "Doc" Plaster, told the band he'd be part of whatever came next if they wanted to carry on.

years.h: Steve Sanderson becomes Gameface's drummer
years.p: Steve Sanderson joins after Three to Get Ready. Jeff Caudill says Sanderson's drumming let Gameface's songwriting expand.

years.h: Jeff Caudill hangs upside down from a hoop in New Bedford
years.p: At a Gameface show in New Bedford, Massachusetts, Jeff Caudill ends up hanging upside down from a basketball rim, the photo fans still pass around. The next night Gameface play CBGB.

years.h: Gameface's Cupcakes 7" and The Reminder
years.p: The Cupcakes 7" (Only Souvenir) comes out, and Dr. Strange collects Gameface's demos and early songs as The Reminder.

years.h: Jeff Caudill picks up a second guitar in Gameface
years.p: Caudill starts playing guitar as well as singing. Revelation's bio says it gave Gameface a fuller, warmer sound.
years.xp: By November 1998 Caudill couldn't picture going back: he said he didn't know what the band had been doing all those years without him on second guitar.

eras.title: The Revelation years
eras.text: On Revelation, Gameface became a touring band: five US tours and one in Europe by the label's count, a Troubadour bill with Jimmy Eat World, and two albums that sit between hardcore, emo and plain good rock songs. It ended with a bassist walking out before a record came out and a drummer leaving for a major label band.

years.h: Gameface, Jimmy Eat World and Sense Field at the Troubadour
years.p: A month before their Revelation debut, Gameface share the Troubadour in Los Angeles with [[Jimmy Eat World|bbc5b66b-d037-4f26-aecf-0b129e7f876a]] and [[Sense Field|8d7bf045-1526-404d-b37c-6f49b714d614]].

years.h: Every Last Time, Gameface's Revelation debut · REV 75
years.p: The first Gameface record with Steve Sanderson and two guitars. Revelation's first vinyl run was just 211 on clear.

years.h: What's Up Bro?, a split 10" with Errortype:11
years.p: Gameface share a 10" with Errortype:11 on Revelation, pressed once: 330 on opaque orange.

years.src: No Echo · AllMusic · Revelation Records pressing history
years.h: Always On · Revelation REV 99
years.p: Gameface's second Revelation album. Bassist Paul Martin quits after recording it and before it comes out.
years.xp: That left a hole when it came time to promote the record. Guy Julian, who officially joined in May 2001, is the bassist in the Always On music video even though he doesn't play on the album.

years.h: Guy Julian joins Gameface on bass
years.p: Guy Julian replaces Paul Martin. Gameface's Feels a Lot Better EP comes out on Firefly Recordings the same year.

years.h: Steve Sanderson leaves Gameface for Instruction
years.p: Before Four to Go comes out on Doghouse Records, drummer Steve Sanderson leaves to join Instruction, then signed to Geffen.

years.h: Gameface go on hiatus
years.p: After Four to Go, Gameface stop. Jeff Caudill later said he'd put so much emotional stock in the band that it felt like part of him.

eras.title: Now is what matters now
eras.text: A Revelation birthday party brought Gameface back. The album that followed was written while Jeff Caudill's father was dying, with old friends from Big Drill Car and Sense Field singing on it.

years.h: Gameface reunite for Revelation's 25th anniversary
years.p: Gameface play night zero of Revelation Records' 25th anniversary shows at the Glass House in Pomona, their first show since 2003.
years.xp: Jeff Caudill told the Washed Up Emo podcast in October 2012 that the band had needed the years apart to get used to having each other in their lives again.

q: That's the best and most concise album Gameface has ever done.
years.h: Now Is What Matters Now · Equal Vision
years.p: Gameface's first album in eleven years. Jeff Caudill wrote Come On Down while his father was dying of lung cancer.
years.xp: Frank Daly of [[Big Drill Car|15689186-1537-445b-a659-dbb071416e6c]] and Jon Bunch of [[Sense Field|8d7bf045-1526-404d-b37c-6f49b714d614]] sing on the record. Caudill doesn't hedge about where it ranks.

years.h: I Owe You One 7": Gameface back on Revelation
years.p: Revelation presses Gameface's I Owe You One 7" as REV 179: 330 on black and 545 on opaque yellow.

eras.title: Thirty years on, still writing
eras.text: Three decades after Three to Get Ready, Caudill and Trout were still telling Bob Binckley's story in interviews, and Gameface were still putting out new songs.

years.h: Jeff Caudill and Todd Trout look back at Three to Get Ready
years.p: For the album's thirtieth anniversary, Caudill and Trout sit down with Dying Scene to talk about Bob Binckley and the record Gameface made after losing him.

years.h: All My Friends EP · Iodine Recordings
years.p: Two new Gameface songs, All My Friends and Men of Stone, written by Jeff Caudill for friends going down rabbit holes or facing failing health.
